hypotheses.reasoning: Starting at 14:56:14, every event-processor crash happens on the same message, msg-476560 at offset 720765, with a recursion or stack overflow in expandReferences (#2908, #2968, #3062, #3240). The offset never commits, so each restart reads the same message and crashes again. Restarts 1 to 4 have doubling backoff (#2910, #2970, #3067, #3241), which is the CrashLoopBackOff in the alert, and because nothing is being consumed, events.raw lag keeps climbing. Before the bad message, batches processed normally. The errors in metrics-agent, report-cron and api-gateway are unrelated background noise.

v4.13.7 rolled out at 14:54:02 and was ready at 14:54:22, about 2 minutes before the first crash. If the new version changed how expandReferences handles recursion, it could be part of the cause. But it processed about 30 batches cleanly afterwards, and the crash is tied to one specific message, which points to the message content rather than the release.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or dead-letter msg-476560 by moving the event-processor consumer group past offset 720765 so the backlog can drain. Look at the payload, which probably contains cyclic or very deeply nested references. Then add cycle detection and a depth limit to expandReferences, and catch per-message errors and send them to a DLQ instead of crashing the process. Check whether v4.13.7 changed expandReferences, and roll back if it did.
